To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is a significant forgetting of actions by elderly adults, and that this forgetting occurs at the same rate as that for young adults.
the elderly are impaired relative to young adults in their ability to learn and recall the content of actions, but that the elderly are not more susceptible to forgetting than young adults.

the memory and retention for action content is impaired in the elderly and that this deficit is not affected by variation in the external context of the actions from the time of their performance to the time of their recall.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of aging on memory and, specifically, on the memory of the content of action.
the effects of variation in external context on the recall and recognition of the content of action.
the effects of age on the acquisition, retention, and recognition of actions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

adult age differences in memory for the content of actions are not due to the variation of the external physical context of the actions from the time of their performance to the time of their memory testing.
there is no evidence for a context-dependent memory deficit in old age.
the memory for the content of actions is not affected by changes in the physical context of the action and that the memory for action content is not affected by adult age differences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no effect of age or of variation in external context on action memory.
there are no age-related differences in the memory and retention for the content of actions in a physical context that varied from that of performance.
age differences in action recall and recognition are not affected by variation in the physical context of action performance and retention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the elderly are not necessarily more sensitive to context changes than the young.
the elderly do not show a significant deficit in action memory.
there are no adult age differences in the memory and retention for the content of actions, even when variation in external context is controlled.
